items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Purge retired Codex MCP tables during migration**

On any workstation that applied the parent revision, this empty manifest does not remove the six existing `[mcp_servers.*]` tables: `modify_private_config.toml` preserves every current table absent from the new managed baseline. Thus `make update` leaves the old MCP definitions in `~/.codex/config.toml`; in particular, a locally enabled legacy server remains enabled and can continue to start despite this change intending to retire it. Add an explicit migration/removal path for these managed legacy table names rather than relying on the generated baseline alone.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L12-L12](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/526dd18b89765d6f53387e63619d759781788cc7/AGENTS.md#L12-L12)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve customized disabled MCP entries**

The new migration treats any table whose name matches a retired server and contains `enabled = false` as the old managed definition. A user who replaced `mcp_servers.github` (or another listed name) with a custom local or remote server but deliberately keeps it disabled will lose the entire entry on the next `chezmoi apply`, even when its command or URL differs from the former baseline. Match the prior managed table fields, or use a migration marker, before purging so disabled user configuration is retained.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:asks to keep customised disabled copies of the six retired tables, but while managed every apply replaced those tables wholesale with the disabled baseline chunk, so none can exist; the purge matches name plus enabled = false only and keeps re-enabled tables, and a disabled server has no effect
